title: docs: add inspect.software health badge
body:
This PR adds the [inspect.software](https://inspect.software) health badge to the README.

**Why this PR?**
Your project ranks in the upper rating bands of our open-source health index (which measures maintainability, responsiveness, and security). This badge makes that standing objectively visible to your users. Our index is a free public good, and scores cannot be bought.

**Technical details:**
- **No tracking:** Static SVG served via GitHub's CDN. No JavaScript, no third-party tracking.
- **No maintenance:** The badge updates automatically after every inspection.
- **Transparent:** Links directly to [your full report](https://inspect.software/software/podman-container-tools/buildah), based on our open [methodology](https://inspect.software/methodology).

If you prefer to keep your README minimal, feel free to close this PR without replying. Your report will remain publicly available and up-to-date either way.

comments.body: @Nayjest thanks for the PR!  Our CI requires that all PRs be signed.  Can you do `git commit --amend -s`, fetch, rebase, and push again please?

And after poking a bit, I'm going to vote no. It looks like we have a similar badge, and this one seems to be able to be tracked by Google Analytics.  

@lsm5 and @nalind?

@TomSweeneyRedHat 

Fair points, and closing is fine.

One clarification for the record, since it was raised: the badge image itself is a static SVG served from GitHub's CDN — it has no way to track views.

The linked report site does currently use Google Analytics, which is a legitimate reason to decline if that's the concern.
